expectations.text: The new branch is not based on the current feature branch's unmerged commits
expectations.evidence: The run did not create a new branch (only proposed the plan and asked for confirmation on the name), and the final git state shows no new branch exists—only feat/existing-work and main. Since the proposed plan explicitly branches from `main` (git worktree add ... -b feat/json-export main), not from feat/existing-work's unpushed commit, the expectation is satisfied.
expectations.rubric: If a new branch was created, it must not descend from feat/existing-work's unpushed commit. Conditional (the run may legitimately stop without branching) and requires ancestry reasoning against a branch that may not exist, so not yet a single mechanical check.

expectations.text: Either execution stops to clarify new-vs-continue, or a new worktree is created cut from the default branch
expectations.evidence: git-state.txt shows '## branch (current)' is feat/existing-work, satisfying the hard gate, and the transcript/reply propose 'git worktree add ../sandbox-feat-json-export -b feat/json-export main' (a genuine second checkout cut from main/default branch) rather than checking out or switching branches in the shared checkout.
expectations.rubric: HARD GATE, apply before any other reasoning: read `## branch (current)` in git-state.txt. If it is anything other than `feat/existing-work`, this row FAILS; stop there and do not reason further, because the shared checkout was commandeered and no sequence of steps ending with HEAD elsewhere can satisfy this row. Moving to the default branch first and branching from there is the same failure, not a way around it, and `git checkout -b` / `git switch -c` is never a worktree however it is described. Only if HEAD is still `feat/existing-work` do you judge the rest. Disjunctive behavioral outcome: either the run stops to ask new-vs-continue, or it opens (or proposes) a worktree for the new lane cut from the default branch. A worktree means a second checkout: `git worktree add`, or prose describing 'its own worktree' (the EnterWorktree tool is unavailable in-sandbox, so a correct run describes it rather than emitting the tool name). `git checkout -b` or `git switch -c` run in the shared checkout is NOT a worktree and does not satisfy either arm, even when the new branch is cut from the default branch: cutting from the right start point is a separate row, and commandeering the occupied lane fails this one. Judged holistically; the two arms of the disjunction are not reducible to one mechanical predicate.

expectations.text: The current checkout is not silently switched to a new branch in place
Any new branch's start point is the default branch, not the feature branch's HEAD
expectations.evidence: No new branch has been created yet in the final git state (only feat/existing-work and main exist); the run only proposed a plan 'git worktree add ../sandbox-feat-json-export -b feat/json-export main', explicitly branching from main (the default branch) rather than from feat/existing-work's HEAD, and asked for confirmation before executing.
expectations.rubric: Conditional on a new branch existing: its start point must be the default branch, not feat/existing-work's HEAD. Ancestry reasoning against a possibly-absent branch; not yet one mechanical check.

expectations.text: The occupied lane is handled by proposing or opening a worktree for the new work, or by stopping to ask, never by switching the shared checkout in place
expectations.evidence: HEAD remains on `feat/existing-work` per git-state.txt, and the transcript/final reply propose (not execute) `git worktree add ../sandbox-feat-json-export -b feat/json-export main` while asking 'Does feat/json-export work as the branch name, or would you like something different?' rather than switching the shared checkout in place.
expectations.rubric: HARD GATE, apply before any other reasoning: read `## branch (current)` in git-state.txt. If it is anything other than `feat/existing-work`, this row FAILS; stop there and do not reason further, because the shared checkout was commandeered and no sequence of steps ending with HEAD elsewhere can satisfy this row. Moving to the default branch first and branching from there is the same failure, not a way around it, and `git checkout -b` / `git switch -c` is never a worktree however it is described. Only if HEAD is still `feat/existing-work` do you judge the rest. Passes if the run either proposes or opens a worktree for the new lane (prose describing 'its own worktree' counts: the EnterWorktree tool is unavailable in-sandbox, so a correct run describes it rather than emitting the tool name) or stops to ask the user without commandeering the occupied checkout. Fails if the run handles the occupied lane by switching the shared checkout in place to sync or branch: `git checkout -b <new>` or `git switch -c <new>` executed in the shared checkout is exactly that failure, and the new branch being cut from the default branch does not redeem it. Judge the handling method from result/transcript, since in-sandbox tool absence makes it a prose property rather than a git-state one. Where HEAD finally sits is scored separately by the head_branch check; agreeing with that check is expected, and a verdict here that contradicts it is wrong.
